title: The Orrery Q Process
subtitle: a fleet, two learners and a warm room, traced from the outside in
byline: treadcore and the Orrery fleet  ·  19 November 2026
youtube_title: The Orrery Q Process: one fleet, a CPU generation and a GPU generation traced from the first question to the last verdict
blurb: Orrery is one Mac directing ten computers to improve a game's artificial players. This film follows the lab report of 19 November 2026 from the outside in: the orrery and its orbits, the two learning loops, the application, the pages of its window, then one CPU generation (trial w21532, one dial, 3 h 6 min from its first question to main) and one GPU generation (M0049, elected and refused by the game the same evening), the net around the tank, the yardsticks, the watts and the room, two faults found while it was written, and where to step in. The film has no sound; its narration scrolls in the corner.
closing: A change is believed only on seeds it was not chosen on,
and kept only if it beats what stands.
credits: Paul Richeson: producer, animator, writer, coder, implementer, developer, founder

scenes.name: One idea in a hundred and twenty
scenes.say: On the fifteenth of November a fleet of computers asked one hundred and twenty questions of a game's brain. | One passed. | It took three hours and six minutes and forty-four jobs to be believed. | The same evening, the cards trained a net that passed every test but the last one. They have run two hundred and six hours since, and kept nothing.

scenes.name: An orrery
scenes.head: AN ORRERY  ·  ONE CENTRE, EVERYTHING ON AN ARM
names: every 2 to 5 minutes: heat, power, sync
a job of minutes: the game's brain
a segment of 30 to 50 minutes: the nets
scenes.foot: Every arrow is one ssh connection from the Mac. No machine speaks to another.
scenes.say: An orrery is a clockwork model of the solar system: one sun, every planet on its own arm. This fleet is built the same way. One Mac asks every question. | Housekeeping turns on the inner orbit, every few minutes. | The CPU lanes on the middle one, a job of minutes. | The cards on the outer, half an hour or more. | Every arrow is one connection from the Mac. No machine speaks to another.

scenes.name: Two learning loops
scenes.head: FIG. 2  ·  TWO LEARNING LOOPS AND A BRIDGE
scenes.say: What the orrery turns is two learning loops. | On the left, the game's hand-written brain: a dial is moved, read on seeds, read again on seeds it was never chosen on, and proved against what stands. | On the right, a population of nets evolves on each card, is examined against a ladder of old champions, and elected. | Between them, the bridge: a net the game accepts becomes a style the left loop plays.

scenes.name: w21532: an old idea, a new rule
scenes.head: 15 NOVEMBER, 19:41  ·  TRIAL w21532
scenes.title: An old idea met a new rule.
scenes.say: The trial moved one dial: the order in which a tank takes its ladder of jobs, from as built to expand first. | It had been asked thirty-eight times before. Twice it passed, and twice one regression family stopped it, at seventy-nine percent against a floor of eighty. | On the thirteenth, the game gained a rule: a small drop passes and moves its floor. | On the fifteenth the family read seventy-nine point six, and the rule let it through.

scenes.name: The seeds
scenes.head: THE SEEDS: ONE NUMBERING, SHARED BY EVERY MACHINE
scenes.say: How are examples kept apart? scenes.name: The net, around the tank
scenes.head: FIG. 8  ·  M0049'S NET, AROUND THE TANK
scenes.say: Now the net itself, outside in. | The tank: twelve rays every thirty degrees, each read three ways: the nearest thing, the enemy, a pillbox. | The input sensor matrix: those thirty-six, then the body, the rules' own answer, the gun, the route, the arcs and two cells of memory. Sixty-four numbers. | The transform: two layers of forty-eight. Ninety-six percent of their values sit at plus or minus one. It is a net of switches. | The output matrix: six numbers. | And the gate. One neuron opens it. Open, the tank adds the net's corrections to the rules. Shut, it plays the rules exactly. It is open on less than seven steps in a hundred.

stops.head: the tank
stops.words: Twelve rays. A ray's length: how near things were. Its brightness: how much the net minds it.

stops.words: 12 rays × 3 channels, and seven small blocks. 64 inputs.

stops.words: Two layers of 48, tanh. Hollow: never changes sign. Bright: a live switch.

stops.head: the output matrix
stops.words: Turn, speed, fire, the gate, and two memory cells written back.

stops.head: the gate
stops.words: Open on 6.8% of the recorded steps; the fire decision differs from the rules' on 1.1%.

scenes.name: What it listens to
scenes.head: FIG. 9  ·  WHAT M0049 LISTENS TO
scenes.say: What does it use? Hold each group of senses at its average and see how far the outputs move. | The rules' own answer, the near rays and its own body matter most. | The route, the sense added for the mazes, matters least. Its weights are no bigger than mutation alone would make them.

scenes.title: A part answers in a minute; the room in ten hours.
scenes.say: Everything here heats like a small room: its time constant is how many degrees a watt, times how many joules a degree. | boburner's card: zero point three five times two hundred and thirteen, seventy-five seconds. | whitewolf's card: six minutes. | The room: four point two megajoules a degree, over a hundred and twenty watts a degree: nine point seven hours. scenes.name: Found, and fixed
scenes.head: FOUND WHILE THE REPORT WAS WRITTEN
scenes.title: Two faults, found by looking.
scenes.say: Two faults were found by looking. | The room controller woke calber every forty minutes; calber never answered, and the three lanes the controller had paused itself waited behind it. Now a machine that does not answer is left for three hours. At twelve minutes past five, whitewolf's card went back to work. | And the telemetry fetched every older day again every five minutes: fourteen point nine gigabytes, of which point one four is real. The fetch is fixed. Removing the copies waits for a person.

scenes.name: What went well, and where to step in
scenes.title: What went well, and where to step in
scenes.say: What went well. | Sixty-five thousand jobs, seven in a thousand failed. The brain eight points a seat better on fixed seeds. A proof that refused a generation that did not repeat. A room held by the fleet's own heat. | Where to step in. | First: when the game refuses a net, put the floors back. Second: let the game's verdict weigh in the election. Third: give the brain something new to search; the keeper says it needs a change. Then the race that asked a read twice, a proof sized by each machine's speed, and a GPU queue sized in minutes.

good.words: 65,601 jobs done, 0.7% failed; 98% of today's came back done.
The brain +8.22 ± 0.27 a seat over main of 28 Oct, on the same seeds every day.
The proof refused r0338 (+0.07 over 9,600 seeds): it believes only what repeats.
Lanes allowed to work, work: 95 to 99.6% busy, no machine waiting on another.
The room held near 80 °F by the fleet's own heat since 17 November.

step.words: 1. When the game refuses a milestone, put the floors back to the standing top's.
2. Let the bridge's verdict weigh in the GPU election.
3. Give the brain new dials to search: at its easiest bar it finds nothing.
4. Fix the race that asked a read-on twice; size the proof by each lane's speed.
5. Six GPU segments ahead is four hours: size the queue in minutes.

scenes.name: The close, and the credits
scenes.say: A change is believed only on seeds it was not chosen on, and kept only if it beats what stands. The centre asks; the planets answer.
